description: Challenge B1 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Fabric has the stressed short /æ/ vowel. Fever has /i/, funnel has /ʌ/, and finish has /ɪ/.
Endeavor has /ɛ/ in its stressed second syllable. Endower has /aʊ/ in that position, indoor has /ɔ/, and endure has /ʊ/.
Compass has /ʌ/ in its first syllable in General American. Campus has /æ/, composed has /oʊ/, and compost has /ɑ/.
Pseudonym begins with /s/ because the initial p is silent. Pneumonia begins with /n/, pterodactyl with /t/, and pharmacy with /f/.
Pneumonia begins with /n/ because its written p is silent. Pterodactyl begins with /t/, phenomenon with /f/, and pseudonym with /s/.
Wrinkle begins with /r/ because its written w is silent. Tickle begins with /t/, winkle with /w/, and nickel with /n/.
Sixths ends with the cluster /ksθs/ in careful pronunciation. Sixth lacks the final /s/, sixes ends /ɪz/, and sickles ends /əlz/.
Debt ends with /t/; the written b is silent. Dead ends with /d/, den with /n/, and desk with /sk/.
Worlds ends with /ldz/. Word ends with /rd/, works with /rks/, and worse with /rs/.
Acquaintance is the spoken target. The other real words have clearly different syllable and vowel patterns; the answer is not a choice between alternative spellings of the same sound.
Conscience is pronounced /ˈkɑnʃəns/. Conscious, consequence, and consonance have different endings and vowel/consonant sequences.
Queue is spelled with five letters but pronounced like /kjuː/. Cute begins with the same /kj/ sequence but has a final /t/; quay is /kiː/, and quite is /kwaɪt/.
